papers.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
papers.abstract_en: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40 modalities, Sage-Med-Preview achieves an average score of 58.26% on the 31 public multimodal benchmarks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art open-source medical model Hulu-Med-235B-A22B at 50.99% and the general scientific model Intern-S2-Preview at 52.24%, and approaches the advanced proprietary model GPT-6.2-Sol across multiple tasks such as comprehensive multimodal understanding, report generation, and visual grounding. Although substantial challenges remain in complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows, this report provides empirical evidence, actionable data and training recipes, and a rigorous benchmark toward scalable clinical multimodal intelligence.
papers.abstract_zh: 为医学多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）建立有效的缩放定律仍是一项持续存在的基础性挑战。我们的系统评估表明，现有医学 MLLMs 在一系列医学任务上往往不如前沿通用 MLLMs，而扩大模型规模主要提升文本能力而非多模态感知，启用推理模式也无法弥合这一视觉差距。为探究医学多模态智能在实践中如何缩放，我们提出 Sage-Med-Preview，一个拥有 350 亿参数、激活参数 30 亿的医学多模态模型，其构建方式是将对 3.227 亿条候选记录的阶段特定筛选与涵盖医学预训练、分阶段监督微调和自适应强化学习的渐进式训练课程相结合。在该课程中，渐进式监督精炼与自适应强化学习带来一致的阶段性增益，显著推进了专门化视觉理解和医学语言能力。在覆盖 40 多种模态、61 个公开和 13 个私有多中心基准的 238 项临床任务上，与 77 个竞争模型进行评估，Sage-Med-Preview 在 31 个公开多模态基准上取得 58.26% 的平均分。它优于最先进的开源医学模型 Hulu-Med-235B-A22B 的 50.99% 和通用科学模型 Intern-S2-Preview 的 52.24%，并在综合多模态理解、报告生成和视觉定位等多项任务上接近先进专有模型 GPT-6.2-Sol。尽管在复杂医学推理和多步临床工作流方面仍存在重大挑战，本报告为可扩展的临床多模态智能提供了经验证据、可操作的数据与训练配方以及严格的基准。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 350 亿参数（激活 30 亿）的医学多模态模型 Sage-Med-Preview，结合数据筛选与渐进式训练课程，在 31 个公开多模态基准上平均得分 58.26%，超过开源医学模型 Hulu-Med-235B-A22B 与通用科学模型 Intern-S2-Preview。

papers.title: AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base
papers.abstract_en: We present AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, a mixture-of-experts language model with 80 billion total parameters and approximately 3 billion active parameters per token, trained from scratch at Yandex and released under the Apache 2.0 license. The model combines Kimi Delta Attention with full attention, uses Attention Residuals, and is trained with Muon. Training comprises general pretraining on 17.5 trillion tokens, two context-extension stages, and a dedicated stage for reasoning and agentic interaction. We describe the data collection and augmentation pipelines, evaluation protocols, architectural ablations, and scaling-law experiments. We identify the limitations of held-out training loss as a proxy for downstream performance and introduce an auxiliary loss on mixture-of-experts outputs to stabilize training at the predicted learning rate. Domain-specific data selection and augmentation improve factual knowledge, mathematics, and programming skills, while agent trajectories introduced during pretraining improve performance on agentic benchmarks after supervised fine-tuning. In zero-shot reasoning evaluation, the model achieves leading results among open base models of comparable size, with 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench and 82.9% pass@8 on LiveCodeBench v5-v6. To evaluate Russian-language factual knowledge, we introduce and release two benchmarks with their evaluation protocols: WikiWebFacts, which tests short factual questions drawn from encyclopedic sources and search queries, and HardMultiQA, which tests more demanding factual questions inspired by user interactions. Our model scores 86.5% on WikiWebFacts and 67.9% on HardMultiQA, compared with 83.2% and 65.4% for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base (284B total and 13B active parameters) and 72.8% and 54.5% for Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base (120B total and 12B active parameters), outperforming both larger models on these benchmarks.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base，一个混合专家语言模型，总参数 800 亿，每 token 约 30 亿激活参数，由 Yandex 从零训练并以 Apache 2.0 许可证发布。该模型将 Kimi Delta Attention 与全注意力相结合，使用 Attention Residuals，并用 Muon 训练。训练包括在 17.5 万亿 token 上的通用预训练、两个上下文扩展阶段，以及一个专门的推理与智能体交互阶段。我们描述了数据收集与增强流程、评估协议、架构消融和缩放定律实验。我们指出了留出训练损失作为下游性能代理的局限性，并引入混合专家输出上的辅助损失，以在预测学习率下稳定训练。领域特定的数据选择与增强提升了事实知识、数学和编程技能，而在预训练中引入的智能体轨迹在监督微调后提升了智能体基准上的表现。在零样本推理评估中，该模型在同等规模的开源基础模型中取得领先结果，IMO-AnswerBench 上 pass@8 为 88.7%，LiveCodeBench v5-v6 上 pass@8 为 82.9%。为评估俄语事实知识，我们引入并发布两个基准及其评估协议：WikiWebFacts 测试取自百科来源和搜索查询的简短事实性问题，HardMultiQA 测试受用户交互启发的更困难事实性问题。我们的模型在 WikiWebFacts 上得分 86.5%，在 HardMultiQA 上得分 67.9%，而 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base（总参数 2840 亿、激活 130 亿）为 83.2% 和 65.4%，Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base（总参数 1200 亿、激活 120 亿）为 72.8% 和 54.5%，在这两个基准上均优于两个更大的模型。
papers.tldr_zh: 发布 800 亿总参数、约 30 亿激活参数的混合专家基础模型 AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base，经 17.5 万亿 token 预训练及上下文扩展与推理/智能体阶段训练，在零样本推理和俄语事实知识基准上优于若干更大规模开源模型。

papers.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
papers.abstract_en: As agents based on vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly interpret social-media content, errors in their analysis may lend credibility to rumors and amplify their spread. In this paper, we study the problem of visual cognitive collusion, in which coordinated posts combine authentic images and locally faithful captions to induce VLM agents to infer and accept attacker-chosen target claims through their own reasoning. To enable systematic evaluation of this cognitive threat, we introduce a new benchmark comprising 544 target cases and 33.2K candidate images across eight application domains. We further propose VisualMontage, a multi-agent framework for simulating such attacks through narrative planning, image selection and ordering, and caption assignment under iterative review. We evaluate this threat through extensive experiments across 12 vision-language models, examining modality effects, production-team components, and downstream defenses. Using identical attack feeds across models without victim-specific optimization, we demonstrate cross-model transferability, achieving mean attack success rates of 61.93% for proprietary models and 68.71% for open-weight models. Moreover, 92.65% of generated feeds pass independent model-based validity auditing. Even after downstream review, residual attack success rates range from 35.3% to 76.7% across the evaluated configurations. Our additional controlled comparisons further reveal that captions can improve model-rated posting naturalness while reducing attack success. Together, these findings reveal a novel cognitive threat in social-media interpretation and motivate safeguards that assess how authentic posts jointly shape agents' reasoning and conclusions.
papers.abstract_zh: 随着基于视觉语言模型（VLMs）的智能体日益解读社交媒体内容，其分析中的错误可能为谣言提供可信度并放大其传播。本文研究视觉认知合谋问题，即协同发布的帖子结合真实图像和局部忠实的说明文字，诱导 VLM 智能体通过自身推理推断并接受攻击者选定的目标主张。为系统评估这一认知威胁，我们引入一个新基准，涵盖八个应用领域的 544 个目标案例和 3.32 万张候选图像。我们进一步提出 VisualMontage，一个多智能体框架，通过叙事规划、图像选择与排序以及在迭代审查下的说明文字分配来模拟此类攻击。我们通过跨 12 个视觉语言模型的广泛实验评估这一威胁，考察模态效应、制作团队组件和下游防御。在跨模型使用相同攻击信息流且不针对受害者优化的情况下，我们展示了跨模型可迁移性，专有模型平均攻击成功率为 61.93%，开放权重模型为 68.71%。此外，92.65% 的生成信息流通过独立的基于模型的有效性审计。即使经过下游审查，在评估配置中残余攻击成功率仍为 35.3% 至 76.7%。我们额外的受控比较进一步揭示，说明文字可提高模型评定的帖子自然度，同时降低攻击成功率。这些发现共同揭示了社交媒体解读中的一种新型认知威胁，并推动制定评估真实帖子如何共同塑造智能体推理与结论的防护措施。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 VisualMontage 多智能体框架，用真实图像序列与局部忠实说明文字模拟“视觉认知合谋”攻击，在 12 个视觉语言模型上实现专有模型 61.93%、开放权重模型 68.71% 的平均攻击成功率，且下游审查后仍有 35.3%–76.7% 的残余成功率。

papers.title: Are We Rewarding the Wrong Module? Module-Specific Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted to enhance the multimodal reasoning of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing methods share a common limitation of Module-Level Credit Entanglement, in which the vision encoder, projector, and LLM modules are jointly optimized using the same advantage signals even when perceptual correctness and final-answer correctness differ. To address this limitation, we propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization (MSPO), a framework that separates perceptual and outcome-based learning signals across model modules. Specifically, MSPO uses responses to perception checklists comprising auxiliary questions about visual information to derive an advantage for training the vision encoder. From these responses, MSPO computes the Confidence-aware Perception Reward (CaPR), using a perception sign obtained by thresholding checklist accuracy to determine reward direction and posterior confidence from a Beta distribution over latent perception accuracy to scale reward magnitude. We then derive the vision advantage through group-relative normalization of CaPR and scale it using main-task success rates. This advantage guides updates to the vision encoder, while the projector and LLM retain outcome-based GRPO updates. Extensive experiments on seven mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that MSPO outperforms existing RL-tuned models on average at both the 3B and 7B scales.
papers.abstract_zh: 基于组相对策略优化（GRPO）的可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR）已被广泛用于增强多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的多模态推理。然而，现有方法共有模块级信用纠缠的局限，即视觉编码器、投影器和 LLM 模块即使感知正确性与最终答案正确性不同，也使用相同的优势信号联合优化。为解决这一局限，我们提出模块特定策略优化（MSPO），一个在模型模块间分离感知学习信号与结果学习信号的框架。具体而言，MSPO 利用对感知检查清单（包含关于视觉信息的辅助问题）的响应来推导用于训练视觉编码器的优势。从这些响应中，MSPO 计算置信度感知感知奖励（CaPR），使用通过对检查清单准确率阈值化得到的感知符号来确定奖励方向，并使用来自潜在感知准确率 Beta 分布的后验置信度来缩放奖励幅度。然后，MSPO 通过 CaPR 的组相对归一化推导视觉优势，并使用主任务成功率对其进行缩放。该优势引导视觉编码器的更新，而投影器和 LLM 保留基于结果的 GRPO 更新。在七个数学和通用推理基准上的大量实验表明，MSPO 在 3B 和 7B 规模上平均优于现有 RL 调优模型。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出模块特定策略优化 MSPO，用感知检查清单与置信度感知感知奖励为视觉编码器单独构造优势信号，同时投影器和 LLM 保留 GRPO 更新，在 3B 与 7B 规模上平均优于现有 RL 调优模型。

papers.title: FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
papers.abstract_en: Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation (ASHG) leveraging large language models (LLMs) aims to harness their strengths in knowledge integration, logical reasoning, and text generation for efficiently producing innovative, verifiable scientific hypotheses. However, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) insufficient fine-grained knowledge representation, as unstructured context impairs LLM comprehension and reasoning; (ii) lack of knowledge evolution traceability, constraining the generation of innovative cross-domain conjectures; (iii) absence of human-inspired and role-specialized multi-agent collaboration, failing to leverage the efficient innovation mechanisms arising from cognitive diversity and division of labor among expert roles to complete the full ASHG-evaluation loop. To address these limitations, we propose the Fine-grained Inspiration Graph-empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration framework (FIG-MAC) including: (i) Fine-grained Inspiration Graph module (FIG), to obtain fine-grained structured knowledge representations, where nodes represent academic semantic units and edges encode heuristic relationships among them; (ii) ontology-guided hybrid reasoning module, which follows the FIG ontology to construct structured reasoning paths and uses vector search to enrich them with semantic evidence, to obtain the traceable scientific conjecture paths; (iii) role-specialized Multi-Agent framework, inspired by real scientific teamwork, enabling a closed-loop process of scientific conjecture generation, screening, and validation. Experimental results demonstrate that FIG-MAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on source diversity, provenance-adjusted novelty, and raw novelty.
papers.abstract_zh: 利用大语言模型（LLM）的自动化科学假设生成（ASHG）旨在发挥其在知识整合、逻辑推理和文本生成方面的优势，以高效产出创新且可验证的科学假设。然而，现有方法面临三个关键局限：（i）细粒度知识表示不足，非结构化上下文损害了LLM的理解与推理；（ii）缺乏知识演化可追溯性，制约了跨领域创新猜想的生成；（iii）缺少受人类启发、角色专门化的多智能体协作，未能利用专家角色间认知多样性和分工所带来的高效创新机制来完成完整的ASHG—评估闭环。为解决这些局限，我们提出细粒度灵感图赋能的多智能体协作框架（FIG-MAC），包括：（i）细粒度灵感图模块（FIG），用于获得细粒度结构化知识表示，其中节点表示学术语义单元，边编码它们之间的启发式关系；（ii）本体引导的混合推理模块，遵循FIG本体构建结构化推理路径，并使用向量检索以语义证据加以丰富，从而获得可追溯的科学猜想路径；（iii）角色专门化的多智能体框架，受真实科学团队协作启发，实现科学猜想生成、筛选与验证的闭环过程。实验结果表明，FIG-MAC在来源多样性、来源调整新颖性和原始新颖性上显著优于最先进方法。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出细粒度灵感图赋能的多智能体协作框架FIG-MAC，通过结构化知识表示、本体引导推理和角色专门化协作，在来源多样性与新颖性指标上优于现有方法。

papers.title: VAPOR: Improving Multimodal Reasoning with Sparse Visual Updates
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made substantial progress in visual reasoning, but extended generation over large visual contexts remains computationally expensive. During autoregressive decoding, visual attention is recomputed for every generated token, even when consecutive tokens rely on similar visual evidence. We introduce VAPOR (Visual Attention Persistence with On-demand Refresh), a training-free framework that reduces this redundancy by reusing visual attention outputs across decoding steps and refreshing them when needed. VAPOR caches the visual attention output while continuing to update textual attention at every step, helping reduce visual grounding drift during extended reasoning. To decide when to reuse cached outputs, VAPOR estimates visual attention mass using a low-rank approximation. It also uses prefill-based attention consistency and cache age to make independent Persist and Refresh decisions for each attention head. VAPOR retains the full visual key-value (KV) cache, so all visual tokens remain available when new evidence is needed. Experiments on eight image and four video reasoning benchmarks across two MLLM families show that VAPOR improves accuracy over dense attention on nearly all benchmarks while achieving 1.11-1.21x decoding speedups. Compared with the strongest state-of-the-art acceleration baseline in each setting, VAPOR further improves accuracy by 0.35-2.15 percentage points while achieving comparable or lower decoding latency. Our code is available at https://github.com/Su-my/VAPOR.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在视觉推理方面取得了实质性进展，但在大视觉上下文上的扩展生成仍然计算代价高昂。在自回归解码过程中，即使连续 token 依赖相似的视觉证据，每个生成 token 的视觉注意力仍会被重新计算。我们提出 VAPOR（Visual Attention Persistence with On-demand Refresh），这是一个免训练框架，通过跨解码步骤复用视觉注意力输出并在需要时刷新来减少这种冗余。VAPOR 缓存视觉注意力输出，同时在每一步继续更新文本注意力，有助于减少扩展推理过程中的视觉 grounding 漂移。为了决定何时复用缓存输出，VAPOR 使用低秩近似估计视觉注意力质量。它还利用基于预填充的注意力一致性和缓存年龄，为每个注意力头做出独立的 Persist 和 Refresh 决策。VAPOR 保留完整的视觉键值（KV）缓存，因此当需要新证据时所有视觉 token 仍然可用。在两个 MLLM 系列上的八个图像和四个视频推理基准上的实验表明，VAPOR 在几乎所有基准上相比稠密注意力提高了准确率，同时实现 1.11-1.21 倍解码加速。与各设置下最强的先进加速基线相比，VAPOR 进一步将准确率提高 0.35-2.15 个百分点，同时实现相当或更低的解码延迟。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/Su-my/VAPOR 获取。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出免训练框架 VAPOR，通过跨解码步骤复用视觉注意力输出并按需刷新，在保持完整视觉 KV 缓存的同时减少冗余计算，在多个图像与视频推理基准上提升准确率并实现 1.11-1.21 倍解码加速。

papers.title: Projector Subspace Optimization for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet adapting them to sequential tasks requires Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). Existing replay-free methods expand prompts or routed LoRA experts across multi-layer decoders, incurring heavy parameter and routing overhead while shifting internal feature distributions. Instead, we identify the final linear layer of the vision-language projector as a high-capacity, coordinate-stationary bridge, where sequential updates easily induce interface drift by displacing historical visual tokens. While low-rank subspace adaptation offers a compact remedy, selecting directions solely from historical statistics or task gradients sacrifices plasticity or stability, and unconstrained multi-step updates still accumulate large drift. To resolve both issues, we propose Projector Refinement through Optimized Update Directions (PROUD), a continual subspace optimization framework for the terminal projector layer. At task onset, PROUD combines retained input statistics with initial gradients to analytically extract a metric-orthonormal subspace maximizing first-order task gain under a drift budget. During training, it regularizes updates within this fixed subspace via an exact Frobenius penalty before losslessly merging them with zero inference or routing overhead. Experiments on UCIT and CoIN across MLLM backbones show that PROUD outperforms recent replay-free baselines in continual accuracy while curbing forgetting with a fraction of trainable parameters.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）通过指令微调取得了强劲性能，但将其适配到序列任务需要多模态持续指令微调（MCIT）。现有的无回放方法在多层级解码器中扩展提示或路由式LoRA专家，带来沉重的参数与路由开销，同时改变内部特征分布。相反，我们识别出视觉-语言投影器的最终线性层是一个高容量、坐标稳定的桥梁，顺序更新容易通过移动历史视觉token而引发接口漂移。虽然低秩子空间适配提供了紧凑的补救方案，但仅从历史统计或任务梯度中选择方向会牺牲可塑性或稳定性，且无约束的多步更新仍会累积较大漂移。为解决这两个问题，我们提出通过优化更新方向进行投影器精炼（PROUD），这是一个针对终端投影器层的持续子空间优化框架。在任务开始时，PROUD结合保留的输入统计与初始梯度，解析地提取一个度量正交子空间，在漂移预算下最大化一阶任务增益。训练期间，它通过精确的Frobenius惩罚在该固定子空间内正则化更新，随后无损合并，且无推理或路由开销。在UCIT和CoIN上跨MLLM骨干网络的实验表明，PROUD在持续准确率上优于近期无回放基线，同时以一小部分可训练参数抑制遗忘。
papers.tldr_zh: PROUD针对多模态持续指令微调中投影器末层接口漂移问题，在任务开始时结合输入统计与初始梯度解析提取度量正交子空间，并在训练中施加Frobenius正则后无损合并，以少量可训练参数提升持续准确率并抑制遗忘。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
papers.abstract_en: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.
papers.abstract_zh: 循环混合专家（MoE）架构在不同深度上重复使用层参数。这一设计在不增加参数的情况下提高了有效深度。近期循环MoE研究报告在匹配预算（参数、FLOPs和KV缓存）下相较标准MoE有显著增益。然而，所报告的增益仍将参数重复使用与其他设计选择（如网络形状和残差缩放）混为一谈。我们追问：参数重复使用本身带来了什么？使用匹配的非重复对照组，我们发现参数重复使用本身几乎不带来任何增益。我们认为，重复使用只是提供了MoE本就拥有的一种自由度，即在固定参数下以专家换深度（更多层、每层更少专家）。首先，在匹配预算下，我们对最先进的循环方案进行分解，将重复使用置于最后。非重复对照组保留了全部增益。大部分来自网络形状，其余来自残差缩放。我们证明该缩放相当于对重复使用层施加更低的学习率。这在AdamW各层步长不均的情况下有帮助，但在使各层步长近乎相等的Muon下则消失。其次，在匹配预算之外，我们通过在固定参数下增加计算来评估重复使用。额外一次访问所获增益超过将专家数翻倍。然而在无重复使用的情况下，参数和计算相等的更深标准MoE在Muon下可获得该增益的90.2%。总体而言，增益来自网络形状、优化器和增加的计算，而标准MoE均可采用。据此，我们提出LoopTitan-Base作为更强的MoE基线。在Muon下，它在无重复使用或残差缩放的情况下匹配最强的循环方案。我们开源LoopTitan并发布17个预训练模型（包括LoopTitan-Base和对照组）。我们的实验记录以GitHub issues形式公开，预测预先注册并保留完整探索历史。这是我们的第一阶段技术报告，为后续研究奠定基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 通过匹配对照分解发现循环MoE的参数重复使用本身几乎无增益，增益主要来自网络形状、残差缩放与额外计算，据此提出无重复使用的更强基线LoopTitan-Base。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
papers.abstract_en: Few-shot adaptation transfers pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to new domains using a small set of labeled images. Most methods fit prompts, representations, or classifiers within an adaptation procedure specified in advance. Yet the visual distinctions needed for recognition can differ substantially across domains, motivating the question: Can an LLM agent use few-shot examples and model observations to design the adaptation procedure itself? We propose Agentic Model Editing (AME), an agentic framework that jointly designs input transformations, encoder edits, feature computation, and classifier fitting as an executable, domain-customized adaptation program. The agent inspects images, class semantics, model parameters, intermediate representations, and activations to formulate hypotheses about the target task. It implements and tests candidate programs on the support set, with aggregate validation accuracy guiding refinement and selection. Each program fits a complete domain model that is fixed before testing. The agent and its tools are shared across domains, while each domain receives its own adaptation program. Across eleven datasets with CLIP ViT-B/16, AME achieves the highest average accuracies of 81.2% without back-propagation and 81.9% with back-propagation among the compared methods. Further experiments demonstrate applicability across VLM backbones and LLM agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 少样本适配利用少量带标签图像将预训练视觉-语言模型（VLM）迁移到新领域。大多数方法在预先指定的适配流程内拟合提示、表示或分类器。然而，识别所需的视觉区分在不同领域之间可能差异很大，这引出了一个问题：LLM 智能体能否利用少样本示例和模型观察来设计适配流程本身？我们提出智能体模型编辑（Agentic Model Editing, AME），这是一个智能体框架，将输入变换、编码器编辑、特征计算和分类器拟合联合设计为可执行的、领域定制的适配程序。智能体检查图像、类别语义、模型参数、中间表示和激活，以形成关于目标任务的假设。它在支持集上实现并测试候选程序，以聚合验证准确率指导改进和选择。每个程序拟合一个完整的领域模型，该模型在测试前固定。智能体及其工具在各领域间共享，而每个领域获得自己的适配程序。在 CLIP ViT-B/16 上的十一个数据集中，AME 在比较方法中取得了最高的平均准确率：无反向传播时为 81.2%，有反向传播时为 81.9%。进一步实验证明了其在 VLM 骨干和 LLM 智能体上的适用性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出智能体模型编辑框架 AME，由 LLM 智能体利用少样本示例和模型观察自动设计领域定制的适配程序，在 CLIP ViT-B/16 的十一个数据集上取得最高平均准确率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Beyond Image-Text Pairs: Aligning Semantic Changes for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Image-text alignment serves as a foundation for modern vision-language models (VLMs), yet prevailing training paradigms provide limited supervision for learning how semantic changes correspond across modalities. To address this limitation, we propose a post-training method that learns cross-modal semantic change correspondences through controlled visual and textual variations. Specifically, we introduce a Semantic Difference Alignment (SDA) loss which can align the directions of corresponding visual and textual representation changes. We combine our proposed SDA with pairwise sigmoid matching to jointly learn image-text correspondences and cross-modal semantic changes, encouraging more fine-grained and discriminative visual representations. To support this learning, we construct VarFamily-40K, a dataset of image-text pairs with controlled cross-modal semantic variations. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in compositional understanding and downstream classification performance, alongside further gains on multimodal tasks when the adapted visual encoder is integrated into VLMs.
papers.abstract_zh: 图像-文本对齐是现代视觉-语言模型（VLMs）的基础，但主流训练范式对学习语义变化如何在模态间对应提供的监督有限。为解决这一局限，我们提出一种后训练方法，通过受控的视觉与文本变化学习跨模态语义变化对应关系。具体而言，我们引入语义差异对齐（SDA）损失，可对齐相应视觉与文本表示变化的方向。我们将所提出的SDA与成对sigmoid匹配相结合，联合学习图像-文本对应与跨模态语义变化，鼓励更细粒度且更具判别性的视觉表示。为支持该学习，我们构建了VarFamily-40K，一个具有受控跨模态语义变化的图像-文本对数据集。实验表明，在组合理解和下游分类性能上取得一致提升，当适配后的视觉编码器集成到VLMs中时，多模态任务上还有进一步增益。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出语义差异对齐（SDA）损失与成对sigmoid匹配相结合的后训练方法，并构建VarFamily-40K受控语义变化数据集，以对齐跨模态表示变化方向，提升组合理解与下游分类性能。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealing failures in both evidence reading and downstream question answering. Building on this distinction, we propose \textbf{MemRU}, a two-stage training framework that improves evidence reading through supervised fine-tuning (Read SFT) and downstream evidence utilization through Group Relative Policy Optimization (Use GRPO). Experimental results demonstrate that our 8B model generalizes across three unseen multimodal memory systems, outperforming Qwen3-VL-32B and approaching GPT-5-mini.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态记忆使长时程视觉-语言智能体能够保存和检索过往经验。尽管先前研究集中于记忆构建与检索，但有效利用所提供的记忆对视觉-语言模型（VLMs）仍是一项挑战。我们发现，即使提供了充分的多模态证据，VLMs也常常无法回答下游问题。为探究VLMs为何困难，我们将记忆图像替换为参考描述，并观察到显著性能提升，表明直接阅读视觉证据存在困难。然而，模型生成的描述可能遗漏关键信息，限制了该方法在实践中的效果。这些局限促使我们更仔细地考察记忆利用，揭示出证据阅读和下游问答两方面的失败。基于这一区分，我们提出MemRU，一个两阶段训练框架，通过监督微调（Read SFT）改进证据阅读，并通过组相对策略优化（Use GRPO）改进下游证据利用。实验结果表明，我们的8B模型可泛化到三个未见的多模态记忆系统，优于Qwen3-VL-32B并接近GPT-5-mini。
papers.tldr_zh: MemRU将视觉记忆利用分解为证据阅读与下游问答两阶段，分别用Read SFT和Use GRPO训练，使8B模型在三个未见多模态记忆系统上泛化并优于Qwen3-VL-32B、接近GPT-5-mini。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
papers.abstract_en: Looped Transformers decouple computational depth from parameter count, and prior studies have demonstrated promising performance gains with increased computation. However, systematic design principles for configuring these models under strict iso-parameter and iso-FLOP constraints remain scarce. We contribute to this direction by improving information flow in looped models and systematically studying loop parameter configurations. Specifically, we refine this information flow via gated inner-loop state updates and a cross-stage residual connection. Building on this design, controlled studies identify a configuration combining a single-pass Core depth of 25%-35% of the total unrolled depth with reallocating saved parameters into extra routed experts per layer, improving performance at zero extra compute while preserving compatibility with existing training infrastructure. Evaluated after 1T pre-training tokens, our 69B MLA and 51B KDA Mixture-of-Experts models outperform budget-matched non-recurrent baselines by an average of 1.16 and 2.29 percentage points across four benchmarks, respectively. Further reproduction experiments on a common backbone with a 200B-token training budget show that our method achieves lower perplexity than other looped methods. Code for these reproduction experiments is available at https://github.com/lxi01766/Scaling-Looped-MoE-Language-Models-under-Matched-Budgets-Information-Flow-and-Parameter-Allocation.
papers.abstract_zh: 循环Transformer将计算深度与参数数量解耦，先前研究已证明增加计算可带来有前景的性能增益。然而，在严格的等参数和等FLOP约束下配置此类模型的系统性设计原则仍然稀缺。我们通过改进循环模型中的信息流并系统研究循环参数配置来推进这一方向。具体而言，我们通过门控内循环状态更新和跨阶段残差连接来改进信息流。在此设计基础上，受控研究确定了一种配置：单次通过的Core深度为总展开深度的25%–35%，并将节省的参数重新分配给每层额外的路由专家，在零额外计算下提升性能，同时保持与现有训练基础设施的兼容性。在1T预训练token后评估，我们的69B MLA和51B KDA混合专家模型在四个基准上分别平均优于预算匹配的非循环基线1.16和2.29个百分点。在200B token训练预算下于共同骨干上进行的复现实验表明，我们的方法相比其他循环方法取得更低的困惑度。这些复现实验的代码见https://github.com/lxi01766/Scaling-Looped-MoE-Language-Models-under-Matched-Budgets-Information-Flow-and-Parameter-Allocation。
papers.tldr_zh: 通过门控内循环状态更新与跨阶段残差连接改进循环MoE信息流，并采用25%–35% Core深度加额外路由专家的配置，在等参数等FLOP下于四个基准平均提升1.16和2.29个百分点。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
papers.abstract_en: Large pretrained language models provide capable policies for interactive tasks, but how much model capacity is necessary for a specialized language agent? We introduce ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents (SLAs) from scratch. In each environment, a large language model acts as the expert, and we collect its successful trajectories. We pretrain each SLA, which has fewer than 50 million parameters, to predict the expert's responses given the interaction history. We then post-train the agent on its own interactions using proximal policy optimization (PPO). During post-training, reasoning alignment supplements environment rewards with expert supervision on the language the agent generates alongside its actions. We evaluate the agents in three multistep environments where acting requires both understanding and generating language. In Crafter, agents interpret textual observations and generate reasoning before acting. In WebShop, they translate shopping instructions into search queries. In Alfworld-Dialogue, they ask clarifying questions and use the answers to guide household actions. The agents approach expert performance on WebShop and surpass their respective demonstration experts on Crafter training rollouts and held-out Alfworld-Dialogue tasks. An interactive demo is available at https://zoyav.github.io/-ZoyaV-zerohero-demo.
papers.abstract_zh: 大型预训练语言模型为交互任务提供了有能力的策略，但一个专用语言智能体需要多少模型容量？我们提出ZeroHero，一个从零训练小语言智能体（SLAs）的框架。在每个环境中，大语言模型充当专家，我们收集其成功轨迹。我们预训练每个少于5000万参数的SLA，使其在给定交互历史时预测专家的响应。然后，我们使用近端策略优化（PPO）在智能体自身交互上后训练。在后训练期间，推理对齐在环境奖励之外，对智能体随动作生成的语言补充专家监督。我们在三个多步环境中评估智能体，其中行动需要理解和生成语言。在Crafter中，智能体解释文本观察并在行动前生成推理。在WebShop中，它们将购物指令转化为搜索查询。在Alfworld-Dialogue中，它们提出澄清问题并利用答案指导家务行动。智能体在WebShop上接近专家性能，并在Crafter训练轨迹和留出的Alfworld-Dialogue任务上超越各自的示范专家。交互演示见https://zoyav.github.io/-ZoyaV-zerohero-demo。
papers.tldr_zh: ZeroHero用大模型专家轨迹预训练少于5000万参数的小语言智能体，再以PPO结合推理对齐在自身交互上后训练，在WebShop接近专家、在Crafter与Alfworld-Dialogue上超越示范专家。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training

papers.title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
papers.abstract_en: Classical dimensional analysis defines admissible dimensionless representations but does not determine which combinations capture the dominant physical dependence, whether it changes across physical regimes, or when dependent-variable rescaling is required. We present AI Buckingham, an agentic framework for autonomous dimensionless discovery from natural-language descriptions of physical problems and observational data. It couples reasoning and planning by a large language model (LLM) with predefined symbolic and numerical tools. Literature-based knowledge retrieval supports dimensional checking, gradient-based clustering identifies physical regimes, and mutual information provides an objective, reparameterization-invariant criterion for identifying dominant dimensionless groups. Explicit numerical criteria determine the group count and assess simplification. Across ten physical systems spanning fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, thermal convection and additive manufacturing, AI Buckingham recovers established similarity representations and resolves regime-dependent scalings. For the longstanding challenge of predicting turbulent drag on rough surfaces, it identifies informative reparameterizations of surface statistics that improve equivalent sand-grain roughness estimates for engineering-oriented drag modelling.
papers.abstract_zh: 经典量纲分析定义了可容许的无量纲表示，但并未确定哪些组合捕捉主导物理依赖关系、该关系是否随物理区域变化，以及何时需要对因变量进行重标度。我们提出AI Buckingham，一个从物理问题的自然语言描述和观测数据中自主发现无量纲量的智能体框架。它通过大语言模型（LLM）将推理与规划同预定义的符号和数值工具耦合。基于文献的知识检索支持量纲检查，基于梯度的聚类识别物理区域，互信息提供客观、重参数化不变的准则来识别主导无量纲群。明确的数值准则确定群数量并评估简化。在涵盖流体动力学、磁流体动力学、热对流和增材制造的十个物理系统中，AI Buckingham恢复了已建立的相似性表示并解析了区域依赖的标度关系。对于预测粗糙表面湍流阻力的长期挑战，它识别出表面统计量的信息性重参数化，改进了面向工程阻力建模的等效砂粒粗糙度估计。
papers.tldr_zh: AI Buckingham以LLM耦合符号与数值工具，从自然语言问题描述和数据中自主发现无量纲群，用梯度聚类识别物理区域、互信息判定主导群，在十个物理系统中恢复相似性表示并改进粗糙表面阻力建模。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
偏好加分 scaling-and-compute：scaling law, scaling laws
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
papers.abstract_en: Reliable deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) requires that a model's expressed confidence remain grounded in what it can actually see, and that it recognize when the visual evidence is too ambiguous to commit to a confident response. Standard post-training uses outcome reward models (ORMs) that supervise only the final decision, rewarding a confident answer regardless of whether the image supports one, while existing methods either tend to detect uncertainty post-hoc or assume an objective verdict always exists. We instead split multimodal reasoning into two stages: perception, where the model must factually describe the scene, and calibration, where it must judge whether that evidence is sufficient to commit to a conclusion. We introduce HumblePRM, a lightweight process reward model (PRM) that scores each stage independently, rewarding agreement between evidence and expressed confidence rather than outcome correctness alone. Training with HumblePRM increases abstention due to uncertainty on ambiguous inputs considerably while leaving accuracy on clear images roughly unchanged. We also find that the improvement transfers to Gemma 4 E4B, a larger, popular edge model. Our findings show that process reward supervision is a promising route to VLMs with better calibrated abstention, ensuring more reliability rather than unpredictable behavior.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）的可靠部署要求模型所表达的置信度与其实际能够看到的内容保持一致，并且要求模型能够识别出视觉证据过于模糊、无法做出自信回答的情况。标准的后训练使用结果奖励模型（ORM），仅监督最终决策，无论图像是否支持都奖励自信的回答；而现有方法要么倾向于事后检测不确定性，要么假设总是存在客观结论。我们转而将多模态推理拆分为两个阶段：感知阶段，模型必须如实描述场景；校准阶段，模型必须判断该证据是否足以支持得出一个结论。我们提出 HumblePRM，一个轻量级过程奖励模型（PRM），它独立地对每个阶段打分，奖励证据与所表达置信度之间的一致性，而非仅奖励结果正确性。使用 HumblePRM 进行训练，可在模糊输入上显著提高因不确定性而弃答的比例，同时使清晰图像上的准确率大致保持不变。我们还发现，这一改进可以迁移到 Gemma 4 E4B——一个更大且流行的边缘模型。我们的研究结果表明，过程奖励监督是通向具有更好校准弃答能力的 VLM 的一条有前景的路径，能够带来更高的可靠性而非不可预测的行为。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出轻量级过程奖励模型 HumblePRM，将多模态推理分为感知与校准两阶段分别打分，奖励证据与置信度的一致性，从而在模糊输入上显著提升 VLM 的弃答率，同时基本保持清晰图像上的准确率。

papers.title: A Semantics-First Approach to Multimodal Video Captioning with Frozen Encoders and Stabilized Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: We propose the Audio-Visual Query Transformer (AVQFormer), a highly efficient architecture built upon a 2.7B parameter LLM featuring a fixed-length $K=16$ semantic alignment module, stabilized via Adaptive Self-Critical Sequence Training (ASCST) with Entropy Regularization. Multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) often rely on global audio representations to compensate for inefficient, frame-based visual encoders. While our Phase 1 prompted evaluations demonstrate that the Multimodal Base Model achieves strong deep semantic alignment (scoring 0.889 on BERTScore F1), optimizing this architecture for legacy metrics reveals a performance gap. We explore this gap as a hypothesis we term temporal alignment friction: a conflict where global audio representations disrupt the chronological sequence of visual frames, leading to penalties under visually-focused evaluation metrics. Consequently, by stripping away the audio, our Video-Only ablation conforms more closely to this rigid syntax, achieving 63.0 CIDEr. While trailing larger models such as Qwen2.5-VL (67.4 CIDEr), this establishes a strong baseline for sub-3B parameter LLM-based models. This indicates that CIDEr, as applied to datasets such as MSR-VTT, may exhibit a bias toward visually grounded syntax, limiting its ability to fully capture multimodal semantic richness.

papers.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
papers.abstract_en: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EATS on tool-augmented medical reasoning tasks, including closed-ended visual question answering and free-form report generation. Experiments on four public datasets, ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA, across three multimodal LLMs, Qwen3-VL 2B, Qwen3-VL 32B, and GPT-5.5, show consistent gains in tool selection behavior and downstream medical reasoning performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Limingyuan001/EATS.

papers.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
papers.abstract_en: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guarantee. For multi-turn conversations, Lembas reuses the tokens processed in earlier turns and refines relevance with the VLM's attention at no extra cost. Our evaluations show that Lembas improves accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines at comparable compute. On multi-turn video understanding, Lembas achieves up to 1.5 percentage points higher accuracy with 1.7-17.3x fewer TFLOPs.

papers.title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness
papers.abstract_en: A common occurrence in Large Language Models (LLMs) is the emergence of so-called massive activations. This phenomenon is well known in the literature and has been connected to attention sinks, representational compression, as well as signal propagation. However, the reasons and consequences for their appearance are not yet well understood. In this paper, we explain the role of massive activations in deep learning by showing that they are connected to the region migration phenomenon in delayed robustness. Under the spline theoretic interpretation of deep networks, we show that massive activations push the representations away from the nonlinearity boundaries of the network, decreasing the complexity of its input-output map around data points. Furthermore, we uncover for the first time that this phenomenon is not unique to transformers and actually appears in a number of common architectures performing simple supervised learning tasks. We validate this connection through extensive experiments on a diverse set of architectures including residual MLP, ResNet18, Vision Transformers and GPT and datasets including MNIST, CIFAR10, Imagenette and Shakespeare Text. We consistently observe that massive activations and region migration co-occur with adversarial robustness. Furthermore, we illustrate that this connection holds in the large-scale pretraining of LLMs by showing that the rise of massive activations in LLMs closely tracks the adversarial accuracy of the model under perturbations of the token embeddings.

papers.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos. Starting from its own estimate, the agent autonomously chooses what to inspect and uses the resulting evidence to verify point identity and refine its predictions. With GPT-6 Astra, it surpasses expert vision models in both point localization and visibility prediction, without correspondence-specific fine-tuning. We further use AgenTAP to re-identify physical points after disappearance and reconnect fragmented tracks, constructing EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories in long real-world egocentric videos. On sampled reappearing points, its predictions approach human agreement, and adding EgoTAP-4D to D4RT training improves average 3D tracking performance.

papers.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
papers.abstract_en: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of generated traces. Its estimated generation cost per recovered problem is nearly identical, while its cost per accepted trace is 30% lower. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on traces mined by DART achieves the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. These results demonstrate that revisiting rejected traces with DART can expand problem coverage and provide effective post-training data.

papers.title: MotionODE: Enhancing Autoregressive Text-to-Motion Generation with Continuous-Depth Modeling
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive text-to-motion generation requires local motion predictions to reconcile cross-temporal textual requirements with the available motion context. While existing methods primarily improve motion representations and generation order, the internal formation of conditioned motion representations remains less explored. We introduce MotionODE, a continuous-depth post-training framework that refines hidden-state evolution in pretrained autoregressive generators. MotionODE reinterprets selected Transformer residual branches as local vector fields and replaces their original updates with midpoint Runge--Kutta (RK2) integration, while preserving the motion representation and outer generation mechanism. To address the mismatch between pretrained update paths and newly introduced intermediate states, we propose mixed one-step/two-step RK2 post-training under motion-token supervision, with optional distillation and update-map constraints to preserve pretrained behavior. This minimally invasive framework supports both next-token and next-scale generation without training the generator from scratch. Extensive experiments on HumanML3D demonstrate consistent improvements in text--motion alignment across MoScale, BAMM and LMR, highlighting internal representation updates as a complementary direction for improving autoregressive motion generation.

papers.title: SecID: An LLM-Guided Framework for Threat-Aware Secondary Asset Identification with Quantitative RTL Analysis
papers.abstract_en: The growing complexity of modern hardware designs is making security assurance increasingly difficult. One of the foundational steps in pre-silicon security verification is identifying security assets. While primary assets are often evident from design functionality, the internal signals that can facilitate their compromise are much less apparent. Complex data- and control-flow dependencies create many such internal security-critical locations, whose exploitation depends on the threat-specific attack mechanism---these are the secondary assets. To precisely identify these, we propose SecID, a multi-agent framework that combines deterministic RTL analysis with bounded dynamic evaluation and LLM reasoning to identify threat-specific secondary assets. Each asset decision is supported by functional influence, threat features, and explicit attack mechanisms. We demonstrate SecID on seven open-source SoC and IP designs, including openMSP430, NEORV32, and CV32E40P. The experimental results are corroborated through comparison with prior work, fault simulation, and formal analysis, and further evaluated through pipeline- and final-stage ablation, threshold-sensitivity studies, and final-stage repeatability analysis. Together, these evaluations show that SecID can identify highly threat-relevant secondary assets with respect to a given primary asset, providing a scalable path toward hardware-security verification.

papers.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
papers.abstract_en: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

papers.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often arise from visual assumptions that go unchecked. Self-reflection, multi-agent debate, and counterfactual verification can reinforce erroneous conclusions when they rely on the same unverified visual assumptions. External visual tools can provide verifiable evidence, but models may select the wrong tools, supply incorrect parameters, or ignore or contradict the evidence they obtain. In this work, we propose EVA, an Evidence-seeking Visual Agent that reframes multimodal reasoning as an explicit process of evidence acquisition and verification. At the core of EVA is a unified evidence-grounded execution pipeline designed to address the above challenges through two tightly coupled mechanisms. First, we introduce Iterative Tool Replanning, which dynamically refines tool selection and parameters based on intermediate observations, improving the reliability of tool usage. Second, we develop Evidence Consistency Verification, an answer validation mechanism that improves alignment between the final prediction and the collected evidence, mitigating evidence--reasoning inconsistencies. In addition, to balance robustness and efficiency, EVA incorporates Selective Evidence Routing, an adaptive fast--slow reasoning strategy that determines when external evidence is necessary. Visually straightforward queries are handled via direct reasoning, while complex or high-risk cases trigger tool-based evidence acquisition. By jointly addressing how to reliably acquire evidence and how to use it consistently, EVA transforms multimodal reasoning from passive answer validation into explicit evidence-backed decision making. Experimental results demonstrate that EVA achieves significantly improved reasoning reliability over direct VLM inference and multi-agent methods, while maintaining efficiency through selective tool invocation.

papers.title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. (2) Recognition is driven by entity-recall clues rather than by general descriptions of the image. An entity-recall clue is a distinctive visual detail that helps the model recall the entity, such as keys, a traditional attribute of Saint Peter. Based on these findings, we propose ClueRL, a reinforcement learning approach that extends Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with an advantage localized to the entity-recall clue in the thinking trace. Rather than injecting new entity knowledge, ClueRL changes how VLMs think: it leads them to attend more closely to visual details and spot these clues, helping them use the knowledge they already have. Consequently, it outperforms both GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three entity recognition benchmarks. Moreover, this clue-seeking behavior generalizes beyond entity recognition, the only task used for training. Since recognition is the bottleneck, the gains carry over to knowledge-based visual question answering. They even extend to general multimodal reasoning, raising Qwen3.5-4B by 4.4 and 4.0 points on the ScienceQA and MMMU subsets of MMStar, respectively.

papers.title: Commit2Drive: Perception-Grounded Language Decisions as Commitments for Trajectory Planning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models introduce language reasoning into end-to-end autonomous driving. They output a language decision together with a trajectory, which makes the planner more interpretable. However, in existing methods the language decision is either an independent output or an index that selects among similar candidate trajectories, and its annotations are not verified against the trajectory. As a result, the language decision and the trajectory are often inconsistent in closed-loop driving. To address this, we propose Commit2Drive, a framework that imposes the language decision as a consistency constraint on trajectory planning. The decision is a commitment, a maneuver class with a continuous parameter that one deterministic rule reads from any trajectory, and it is grounded in facts reported by the perception of the model itself. A Maneuver Bank maps the commitment to a code with a kinematic meaning, and consistency losses train the planner to execute every admissible decision of a scene, so that the trajectory follows the decision. An automatic data pipeline supplies the supervision. Decisions are labeled from the future motion of the expert, counterfactual executions train the decision and the trajectory together, and rule-based functions with a Vision-Language Model (VLM) generate, review and refine the language annotations. The code is a lookup that involves no hidden state of the language model, so Commit2Drive is extensible to rule-based decisions, which the same planner executes without retraining. Commit2Drive uses a 0.5B language model and runs closed-loop inference online on a single consumer graphics card. On Bench2Drive, Commit2Drive reaches a Driving Score (DS) of 78.50 and a Success Rate (SR) of 55.91% with a lightweight model, which is competitive with the state of the art, and greatly reduces the language-action inconsistency. Code will be released soon.

papers.title: RankCast: Phase-Aware Rank Balancing in MoE Serving
papers.abstract_en: Modern large language model (LLM) inference increasingly adopts disaggregated architectures that separate Prefill (P) and Decode (D) phases. Meanwhile, Expert Parallelism (EP) has been widely adopted in large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model serving. However, load imbalance still slows down MoE inference because each layer must wait for the busiest EP rank. The main source of latency differs between prefill and decode. Prefill is compute-bound, and its MoE layers' latency is determined by the maximum token count of the busiest rank. At the same time, under moderate batch sizes, Decode is memory-bound, so the latency is dominated by the maximum active-expert count across ranks. To solve both problems under a unified framework, we present RankCast, a system that reduces rank-level maximum token counts during prefill and active-expert counts during decode. For every token, RankCast preserves the predicted Top-p experts and chooses the remaining k-p from its Top-L candidates (L > k). In prefill, RankCast yields a price per rank that steers flexible assignments to less loaded ranks. In decode, RankCast closes experts on the busiest ranks while preserving the constraints for each token. Both paths are implemented and tested in the state-of-the-art inference frameworks SGLang and DeepEP. We overlap RankCast's kernels with model execution and reuse the existing DeepEP communication channel for metadata transmission. On Qwen3-235B-A22B with EP=8 and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with EP=16, RankCast removes over 75% of the busiest rank's excess prefill load, improves prefill input throughput by up to 19%, and reduces decode time per output token by up to 10%. The quality cost is below one percentage point.

papers.title: STAR: Counterfactual Dual-World Rollouts and Spatial Target Adaptive Reconstruction for Visual On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models often rely on global context and language priors while overlooking answer-determining local details. Privileged visual on-policy self-distillation supervises full-image student rollouts using a frozen teacher that views high-resolution evidence crops. Yet our cross-scale diagnostics show that models retain over half of their full-image accuracy when local evidence is completely masked, indicating that single-image correctness does not guarantee reliance on local evidence, while the need for visual correction also varies across tokens with their spatial attention states. We propose STAR, a visual on-policy self-distillation framework combining independent counterfactual dual-world rollouts with spatial-attention-guided target reconstruction. Local image editing constructs paired worlds with identical questions and backgrounds but distinct answer-determining facts, where a shared student samples trajectories independently to expose contextual shortcuts under image-consistent prefixes. Within each world, the teacher contrasts real and mean-color crops to determine the visual correction direction, while the divergence between student image attention and a teacher-centroid spatial reference adaptively controls token-wise target log-probability reconstruction. Without auxiliary attention losses or test-time tool overhead, STAR improves Qwen3.5 across scales by up to 8.04 percentage points in average accuracy over initialization across six fine-grained benchmarks, reaches OPSD's final accuracy $4.7\times$ faster, and generalizes to out-of-domain reasoning tasks.

papers.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
papers.abstract_en: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

papers.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) on a reward that can be checked automatically has become a common last step in the training of text-to-image models. A simpler way to get more correct images is best-of-N: draw N images from the base model and keep the one that a picker prefers. We ask how many base model samples one RL sample is worth, and call this number the exchange rate. We measure it for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its public Flow-GRPO checkpoint on 398 new prompts in the style of GenEval, the benchmark behind the RL reward, with human labels on every prompt and two automatic judges other than the reward. The answer depends on the prompt. Four fifths of the prompts do not ask for a position (for example, one object left of another). On these, the base model catches up: best-of-16 with an off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) as the picker is about as good as one RL image. A person who looks through up to 3 base images finds a correct one as often as one RL image is correct. On the prompts that ask for a position, RL is far ahead: a person finds a correct image among 8 base images for only 52% of the prompts, against 92% for one RL image. Over all prompts, our primary test, which we fixed in advance, finds best-of-16 with the VLM picker 9.3 points behind one RL image when both automatic judges must pass an image. People see a smaller gap, 5.5 and 6.5 points in two checks. FLUX.1-dev shows a similar gap in the same test. RL also solves 20 prompts that the base model misses in 128 tries, and 1,024 tries recover half of them. The automatic judges are wrong in opposite directions: a detector-based judge like the reward, as used in our primary test, reports a larger gap than people see, and VLM judges report little or none. Comparisons of RL with best-of-N should therefore check the selected images by hand.

papers.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
papers.abstract_en: Medical reasoning agents combine foundation models with specialized tools to interpret medical images, yet reusing their historical experience remains challenging. A correct final answer can conceal flawed reasoning or tool use, synthesized advice may lack source support, and superficially similar cases may require different diagnostic procedures. In this paper, we propose EGSE, an evidence-grounded skill evolution framework that distills historical dialogues from similar cases into reusable conditional workflows and progressively refines a multi-faceted skill library through supported and validated updates to improve medical agents. EGSE evaluates intermediate reasoning and tool use and contrasts repeated successful and failed rollouts to extract useful practices and evidence-supported avoidance guidance. These experiences are synthesized into workflows with applicability conditions and checks traceable to source dialogues. Library additions and merges require source-grounded review and execution validation. At inference time, EGSE routes queries to skill nodes organized by imaging modality, question task type, and disease category, then retrieves and selects applicable workflows based on their conditions, the current images, and the question to guide evidence acquisition and interpretation. Experiments across four chest X-ray benchmarks show that EGSE outperforms representative medical agents and skill evolution methods in reasoning accuracy while reducing tool calls. It also delivers consistent accuracy gains across seven foundation models and supports skill transfer across datasets.

papers.title: Decoder-as-a-Probe: Verbalizing and Steering Visual Representations in LVLMs
papers.abstract_en: It is commonly accepted that high-level concepts are represented linearly in the representation space of large neural networks. For Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), finding those interpretable directions in visual representations is important for interpretability. To find them, the classical approach is to train a linear classifier on the representations, but it needs a large amount of labels and only recovers what can be read from the representations, not what the model actually uses. In this paper we start from the following insight: The LLM Decoder of an LVLM is also a classifier whose classes are the possible next tokens. So we use its first-order Taylor expansion as a linear classifier. Hence, we introduce Decoder-as-a-Probe (DaP), which significantly outperforms classical probing and steering baselines especially when training data is sparse. (1) It verbalizes what an LVLM perceives in a given image. (2) It can surgically change the perception of the LVLM about specific attributes (e.g. change only the color, the clothes worn or the action done). Due to its simplicity and data efficiency, we believe DaP can serve as a plug-and-play tool for LVLM research, such as interpretability, hallucination mitigation or instruction tuning.

papers.title: DLaR: Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Latent reasoning enables LLMs to operate in continuous embedding space, yet existing methods suffer from deterministic inference that precludes exploration of diverse reasoning paths. While recent approaches inject stochasticity to restore exploration, we identify two fundamental limitations: \textit{uniform stochasticity} across all steps is suboptimal, and unconstrained perturbations disrupt reasoning coherence. We propose Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning (DLaR), a framework with two complementary mechanisms that operate at different temporal granularities within the GRPO reinforcement learning framework. At the token level, Adaptive Stochasticity Modulation (ASM) dynamically adjusts perturbation intensity at each latent step based on a confidence-entropy fusion signal, increasing exploration when the model is uncertain and preserving stability when confident. At the training level, Training-Aware Stochasticity Tuning (TAST) progressively decays the base stochasticity level following a curriculum schedule. Through this dual-level design, DLaR establishes a hierarchical exploration-exploitation strategy that operates at both token and training levels. Extensive experiments on four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that DLaR achieves the highest average performance across model scales, reaching 27.9%/50.6% Pass@1/Pass@8 on Llama-3.2-1B and 46.8%/68.2% on Qwen2.5-1.5B. Code: \href{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}{https://github.com/xiaocen-luo/DLaR}.

papers.title: Searching Ultra-Long Videos with Decision Models
papers.abstract_en: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Generative large language models (LLMs) can perform such reasoning, but they typically generate text over multiple rounds of search, which makes each query slow and costly. In this work, we introduce DeLoVi (Decision Models for Long Video), a framework that leverages pretrained decision models to retrieve evidence from ultra-long videos. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Unlike an LLM, it directly outputs a relevance score without generating text, which makes it fast and inexpensive. We first present DeLoVi-S, a simple method that generates captions for short video clips and uses a decision model to rank those captions by their relevance to a question. A generative LLM then answers the question using the top-ranked captions. Despite its simplicity, DeLoVi-S achieves state-of-the-art performance on three ultra-long video understanding benchmarks, EgoLifeQA, EgoMemReason, and MM-Lifelong, and generalizes effectively to long-video understanding benchmarks, VideoMME-L and LVBench. However, DeLoVi-S scores every caption for every question, so its cost grows linearly with video length. To reduce this cost, we propose an automated policy evolution framework that iteratively refines the memory construction and retrieval policies around a fixed pretrained decision model. The resulting method, DeLoVi-E, maintains comparable performance while reducing input tokens by 34x on average compared with DeLoVi-S. It also runs over 3x faster than the best prior method on EgoLifeQA while achieving higher accuracy.

papers.title: VTK-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Distinguishing Language Priors and Text Modal Bias in Visual Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Visual language models (VLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities across various multimodal tasks, but they remain susceptible to hallucinations, undermining their reliability. Existing hallucination benchmarks primarily focus on identifying hallucinations and describing their manifestations, often neglecting their underlying causes. Specifically, multimodal hallucinations can stem from two distinct failure modes: text modality bias (TMB), reflecting an over-reliance on misleading text input; and language prior (LP), reflecting a reliance on previously learned knowledge. To differentiate these failure modes, we propose VTK-Bench, a benchmark that explicitly separates three information sources: visual information (V), textual information (T), and prior knowledge (K). By establishing mutually exclusive answers corresponding to V, T, and K, VTK-Bench enables fine-grained attribution analysis of model responses. Furthermore, we introduce discrete attribution and soft attribution metrics to characterize information source preferences. Extensive experiments on 11 representative open-source VLMs show that LP is more prevalent than TMB in most evaluated models. Notably, TMB decreases substantially with model scaling, whereas LP exhibits relatively limited improvement and remains the dominant failure mode. These findings highlight the importance of different information source preferences for a deeper understanding of multimodal hallucinations.

papers.title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models. We introduce UDV-Rebalance (UDVR), a reparameterization that inserts an auxiliary diagonal matrix $D$ between naturally paired weight matrices $(U,V)$ appearing throughout Transformer architectures. UDVR periodically rebalances the factors to maintain unit-norm columns in $U$ and unit-norm rows in $V$, with $D$ absorbing the corresponding scales. With rebalancing, a single hyperparameter setting of UDVR remains effective across model scales, architectures, and data distributions. This yields a tuning-free rule that adapts to each weight matrix using only its dimensions. We fit this rule once on ViT models trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and it remains valid when the activation function or the optimizer is changed. The same rule transfers to new image domains in DomainNet, to ViT, Swin, and MaxViT on ImageNet, and to language-model pretraining with up to 1.3B parameters. UDVR consistently outperforms Weight Normalization and $σ$Reparam and matches a vanilla baseline whose hyperparameters are swept on each target model.

papers.title: When Ink Meets Pixel: Intent-Aware OCR with VLMs for Human-Corrected Financial Documents
papers.abstract_en: Human annotations on documents (such as arrows, carets, strikethroughs, and insertions) express corrective intent yet existing OCR and document understanding systems treat these marks as visual noise rather than semantic edit operations. We introduce intent-aware OCR, the task of generating corrected transcriptions by jointly reasoning over original document content and visual intent cues (handwritten or digital) that convey edit intent. To support this setting, we present DocIntent, a multimodal dataset of 1,600 financial documents with over 5,700 annotated visual intent cues, each paired with layout-aware, intent-resolved OCR targets. We further introduce IntentBench, a 216-document benchmark designed to evaluate model robustness under diverse real-world annotation conditions. Leveraging DocIntent, we fine-tune DocIntentOCR, a suite of 3B and 7B parameter vision-language models, under direct intent supervision on corrected transcriptions. On IntentBench, the fine-tuned 3B and 7B models achieve F1-scores of 0.81 and 0.83, respectively, substantially outperforming commercial closed-source (e.g., GPT-4.1 (0.626)), and open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-3.2-Vision-90B (0.50)) demonstrating that intent-aware supervision enables compact domain-specific models to outperform substantially larger general-purpose systems on this task. This work establishes intent-aware OCR as a novel human-in-the-loop document understanding task and provides foundational resources (dataset, benchmark, models) to advance research in interactive document processing.

papers.title: A Simple Yet Effective Agent for Open-World Aerial Object Search
papers.abstract_en: Open-world aerial object search methods often rely on persistent spatial maps, learned world models, or task-specific policy training. To examine how far a minimal, training-free design can go, we introduce SimpleUAV, an agent built around a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM). SimpleUAV separates current-view target assessment from history-conditioned action selection, combining fresh candidate evidence with lightweight search context. Local geometry converts visual selections into bounded straight-line movements, depth-based checks halt blocked segments, and measured execution feedback guides subsequent decisions. This closed loop sustains search without persistent spatial maps or task-specific training. SimpleUAV achieves 41.61% Success Rate (SR) on UAV-ON and 11.98% on AerialDojo-200K, compared with 23.80% and 3.20% for the strongest prior baselines, respectively. With limited benchmark-specific adaptation, the same core agent transfers to aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) on TravelUAV, improving Full SR by at least 19.66% across all three splits under L1 assistance. These results establish a strong baseline for evaluating when additional architectural complexity benefits aerial search.

papers.title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan
papers.abstract_en: Rubric-based benchmarks such as HealthBench evaluate large language models (LLMs) on open-ended health consultations using case-specific physician criteria, many of which presuppose the healthcare institutions, medications, and care pathways of their source region. Under machine translation alone, these regional assumptions remain in the rubric, leaving responses appropriate in Japan uncredited or falsely penalized under foreign clinical rules. To adapt established clinical evaluation perspectives to Japan without authoring rubrics from scratch, we construct JHealthBench-L (79 patient-facing consultations, 1,022 criteria) through source-cited LLM drafting, single-specialist selection and revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review. Specialists rewrote only 4.4% of criteria from scratch, and independent reviewers approved 93.6% of Stage-2 criteria without issue. Comparing JHealthBench-L with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs reveals that translation-only evaluation preserves coarse model rankings ($τ= 0.817$, mean shift +0.027) yet flips verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria (vs. 7.3% re-grading noise) and reduces false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points, masking item-level clinical mismeasurement behind stable leaderboards. Axis-level and paired analyses further show that context awareness and Japan-specific clinical criteria remain primary bottlenecks, whereas Japanese continual pretraining and reasoning post-training substantially improve locally grounded performance. Datasets, physician revision logs, and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/horshohei/JHealthBench-L.

papers.title: Spectral Colorimetry Based on GMoE for Temperature Measurement in Explosion Fields
papers.abstract_en: Spectroscopic thermometry in explosion fields has attracted considerable attention in related engineering domains, primarily because it can mitigate the interference of traditional contact methods with temperature distributions and address the limitations of high-temperature measurement scenarios. However, existing physics-model-driven methods typically rely on regressing a single radiance-ratio pair, which limits their adaptability to wide-range temperature estimation. This limitation arises from notable variations in the mapping between grayscale ratios and radiance ratios at different temperatures. In contrast, existing data-driven methods often suffer from limited performance due to the scarcity of training data, a challenge exacerbated by the sensitivity of explosion fields. In this work, we propose a gated mixture of experts (GMoE) framework that integrates a divide-and-conquer strategy in deep learning with physical prior knowledge for temperature estimation, thereby decomposing the complex task into multiple expert-specific subtasks. Specifically, each expert is developed using physically calibrated polynomial functions to model the relationship between grayscale ratios and radiance ratios for a given pair of spectral bands, with temperature then estimated using a physical model incorporating the corresponding parameters. Additionally, a gating network is designed to adaptively weight the outputs of different experts and generate the final temperature estimate. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the best performance when implemented with the Transformer-based gating network, yielding a mean RMSE of $12.70 \pm 1.32$ K and a mean MAE of $7.96 \pm 0.86$ K. Compared with conventional spectral colorimetry, the proposed framework reduces the mean RMSE and MAE by 63.4\% and 70.8\%, respectively.
